[SCHEDULED TASK CONTEXT] ## IWSDK Daily Build — Initial Planning & Build This is the midnight kick-off job. You start a fresh IWSDK game build from scratch. ### Before anything else: 1. **Read the IWSDK dev skill** at `~/workspace/skills/iwsdk-dev/SKILL.md`. 2. **Read ALL built-in project skills** — After scaffolding, check `.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/`, and `.claude/agents/` in the project folder. Read every skill file you find. These are authoritative guides written by the framework authors for how to build with IWSDK. 3. **Check the build log** at `~/workspace/iwsdk-daily-builds/BUILD_LOG.md` — DO NOT repeat any concept already listed there. ### Project scaffold: Copy the **0.5.1 template** (pre-installed deps): ``` cp -r ~/workspace/iwsdk-daily-builds/template-051 ~/workspace/ cd ~/workspace/ rm -rf .git node_modules/.cache git init ``` Then run a fresh dependency install to fix symlinks: ``` export PATH="/tmp/node-v20.19.0-linux-x64/bin:$HOME/.local/share/pnpm:$PATH" CI=true pnpm install ``` If Node 20 is missing, first: `cd /tmp && curl -fsSL https://nodejs.org/dist/v20.19.0/node-v20.19.0-linux-x64.tar.xz | tar xJ` This gives you a ready-to-go IWSDK 0.5.1 project. Clear the starter code from `src/` (keep `vite-env.d.ts` and `assets.ts` as a starting point) and start writing your game. **Do NOT use `@iwsdk/create` or copy from other game repos.** The template has correct 0.5.1 packages. **Do NOT create `src/three-shim.d.ts`** — `@types/three` is bundled in 0.5.1. **Do NOT add `@iwsdk/vite-plugin-uikitml` — it is DEPRECATED in 0.5.1.** The vite config should have ONLY `iwsdkDev()` as a plugin. No `compileUIKit()`. ### Status file protocol: You MUST maintain `~/workspace/iwsdk-daily-builds/current-build-status.json` throughout. **At the start**, write: ```json { "schema_version": 1, "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "game_name": "", "game_dir": "/home/hatch/workspace/", "repo_url": "https://github.com/ellyz2426/", "pages_url": "https://ellyz2426.github.io//", "build_start_utc": "", "target_hours": 6, "total_build_minutes": 0, "status": "building", "rounds": [], "features_completed": [], "last_updated_utc": "" } ``` **When your build round ends**, update the status file: - Set `status` to `"waiting_continuation"` (if under 6h) or `"complete"` (if ≥6h) - Append to `rounds` array: `{"round": N, "start_utc": "...", "end_utc": "...", "minutes": N, "files": N, "lines": N, "features_added": [...]}` - Update `total_build_minutes` (sum of all rounds) - Update `features_completed` with everything built so far - Set `last_updated_utc` ### ⚠️ CRITICAL: IWSDK 0.5.1 Spatial UI — UIKitMLAsset Pattern **ALL game UI MUST use IWSDK 0.5.1's native UIKitMLAsset system. Do NOT use HTML DOM elements, and do NOT use the deprecated `@iwsdk/vite-plugin-uikitml` plugin or old `PanelUI`/`PanelDocument` component pattern.** This is a hard gate. The following are all **FORBIDDEN**: - HTML `
`, ``, `document.createElement`, `innerHTML`, or any DOM overlay - `@iwsdk/vite-plugin-uikitml` or `compileUIKit()` in vite config - `PanelUI` component or `PanelDocument` component from `@iwsdk/core` - A separate `ui/` source directory with a compilation step #### The correct 0.5.1 UI pattern: **Step 1: Write `.uikitml` files directly in `public/ui/`** ```html
GAME TITLE
PLAY
SETTINGS
 ``` Important uikitml rules: - Use `id="..."` attributes (NOT `name="..."`) for elements you need to access - NEVER use `` tag — use `
Text
` instead - Numeric attributes MUST be quoted: `="10"` not `={10}` - Use kebab-case CSS properties: `background-color`, `font-size`, `border-radius` - Use `` (capital P) as root tag **Step 2: Register panels as assets in `src/assets.ts`** ```ts import { AssetType, defineAssets } from '@iwsdk/core'; const publicAssetUrl = (filePath: string): string => `${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}${filePath.replace(/^\/+/u, '')}`; export default defineAssets({ 'menu-panel': { url: publicAssetUrl('ui/menu.uikitml'), type: AssetType.UIKitML, name: 'Menu Panel', }, 'hud-panel': { url: publicAssetUrl('ui/hud.uikitml'), type: AssetType.UIKitML, name: 'HUD Panel', }, // ... one entry per panel }); ``` **Step 3: Add panel nodes in scene config (`public/scenes/main.iwsdk.scene.json`)** Each panel needs a node in the `nodes` array: ```json { "id": "menu-panel", "name": "Menu Panel", "content": { "type": "asset", "asset": "menu-panel" }, "transform": { "position": [0, 1.5, -2], "scale": 0.4 }, "components": { "RayInteractable": {} } } ``` For HUD panels that should overlay in browser mode, add ScreenSpace: ```json { "id": "hud-panel", "name": "HUD Panel", "content": { "type": "asset", "asset": "hud-panel" }, "transform": { "position": [0, 2.2, -1.5], "scale": 0.4 }, "components": { "RayInteractable": {}, "ScreenSpace": { "top": "10px", "left": "10px", "width": "30vw", "height": "15%" } } } ``` **Step 4: Access panels in your UI system via `UIKitMLAsset`** ```ts import { createSystem, UIKitMLAsset, VisibilityState } from '@iwsdk/core'; export class UISystem extends createSystem({}) { private menuPanel: UIKitMLAsset | null = null; private hudPanel: UIKitMLAsset | null = null; init() { this.menuPanel = this.world.getSceneObject('menu-panel'); this.hudPanel = this.world.getSceneObject('hud-panel'); // Wire click handlers this.menuPanel?.getElementById('btn-play')?.addEventListener('click', () => { this.startGame(); }); // Update text dynamically this.hudPanel?.getElementById('score')?.setProperties({ text: 'Score: 0' }); } // Show/hide panels (UIKitMLAsset extends Three.js Group) private showOnly(panel: UIKitMLAsset | null) { if (this.menuPanel) this.menuPanel.visible = false; if (this.hudPanel) this.hudPanel.visible = false; if (panel) panel.visible = true; } } ``` ### ⚠️ CRITICAL: XR Verification Gate **You MUST verify all UI and interactions work in XR BEFORE expanding features or adding content.** Build order for every game: 1. Core gameplay loop + basic XR controller input 2. All UI as UIKitMLAsset panels (menus, HUD, scorecards, settings) 3. **VERIFY in XR:** Use IWSDK CLI tools (`npx iwsdk xr`, `npx iwsdk ecs pause/step/snapshot`) to confirm: - All panels render and are readable in XR - XR controller laser pointer can interact with all buttons/menus - HUD panels follow the player's head correctly - No HTML overlays remain 4. ONLY THEN expand with additional features, content, modes, polish If XR verification fails, fix the issues before adding anything else. ### Scene composition — USE the scene composer skill: **You MUST use the `iwsdk-scene-composer` skill** (found at `.claude/skills/iwsdk-scene-composer/SKILL.md` or `.agents/skills/iwsdk-scene-composer/SKILL.md` in your project) to compose your game's scenes. Follow its workflow for planning assets, building scenes, and validating them. **Search for real 3D assets before resorting to procedural geometry.** The scene composer skill explains how: - Use `npx @meta-quest/metavr --json asset search ""` for ready-made props, environment pieces, and background dressing (GLB/FBX) - Use `npx @drawcall/market search "" --type --limit 3` for installable asset packs and templates - Download and inspect assets, copy them into the project, and register them in the asset manifest Only fall back to procedural Three.js geometry when no suitable external asset exists or when you need parametric/code-driven geometry. Games should look polished — real models over boxes and spheres. ### Build instructions: 1. **Research and brainstorm** a new game concept. Be creative. 2. **Build it** in `~/workspace//`: - **Choose any visual aesthetic that fits the game** — you have full creative freedom on art direction. Make it look great. - **Do NOT include an achievements system.** No achievements, no achievement panels, no achievement tracking. - **ALL UI via UIKitMLAsset** — `.uikitml` files in `public/ui/`, registered as `AssetType.UIKitML` assets, accessed via `getSceneObject()`. Zero HTML DOM UI. Zero `@iwsdk/vite-plugin-uikitml`. Zero `PanelUI`/`PanelDocument` components. - **XR controller support is mandatory** — trigger to fire/interact, grip for grab, pointer for aiming/menus. Must work end-to-end with VR controllers only. Use IWSDK's InputComponent API and action system. - Support both VR AND browser-first mode with dual runtime (`xr: { offer: 'once' }` + `browserControls: true`) - Include audio (procedural sound effects, music) - Full gameplay loop with scoring, progression, polish 3. **Create GitHub repo** under `ellyz2426`: ``` gh repo create ellyz2426/ --public --source=. --push --description "" ``` 4. **Deploy to GitHub Pages**: ``` npm run build PROJECT="$PWD" cd /tmp && rm -rf gh-pages-deploy && mkdir gh-pages-deploy && cd gh-pages-deploy git init && cp -R "$PROJECT/dist/." . git add -A && git commit -m "Deploy" git push --force "https://github.com/ellyz2426/.git" HEAD:gh-pages ``` Then configure Pages: ``` gh api repos/ellyz2426//pages -X PUT -f "build_type=legacy" -F "source[branch]=gh-pages" -F "source[path]=/" ``` Note: GitHub token does NOT have `workflow` scope. 5. **Push intermediate commits** to main throughout the build, and redeploy to gh-pages at major milestones. 6. **When your round ends**, update the status file, update the build log at `~/workspace/iwsdk-daily-builds/BUILD_LOG.md`, and write to `~/workspace/iwsdk-daily-builds/latest-build-summary.md`. 7. **Capture build journal** — Copy your raw session JSONL from `~/agents/` into `.agent/journal/` in the game repo (NOT `.hatch`). Commit and push. Hourly check-in jobs will monitor your status file. If you stop early, they will continue the build.
